cancellation.value: The dedicated policy now says cancellation is effective when the request is received, with no retention conversation or administrative approval required. A request received before charge submission stops that charge; later requests stop future renewals and trigger review of the current payment under refund rules. The old 48-hour notice rule is not carried forward. Canceling renewal does not itself end a prepaid current term or refund a processed payment. Before Medication Fulfillment Start, the policy provides a full affected-payment refund unless a separately itemized and accepted service fee applies; after that point, completed services and pharmacy-started medication are nonrefundable except as legally required, with objectively unearned portions refundable. Terms-of-use wording about intake-stage consultation refunds conflicts and is retained separately, not resolved here.
cancellation.quote:
**Your cancellation is effective at the timestamp our system receives the online request, email, telephone request, or voicemail.** No retention conversation or administrative approval is required. Online and email submissions receive an immediate automated receipt; final confirmation is sent within one business day.

A request received before a scheduled charge is actually submitted will stop that charge. If the charge was already submitted before cancellation became effective, cancellation stops later renewals and the current payment is reviewed under the refund rules below.

current_term_evidence.quote: Canceling automatic renewal stops the next prepaid-term charge but does not, by itself, terminate the Current Term.
